results.title: Top 7 Robinhood Chain RPC Providers in 2026 | Chainstack
results.content:
Pricing is request-unit (RU) based and transparent: a free Developer tier includes 3M RU/month at 25 RPS, Growth is $49/month for 20M RU at 250 RPS and is where archive data and debug/trace access turn on, and Dedicated Nodes become available starting on the $199/month Pro plan. Debug and trace methods additionally require the node to be deployed as a Global Node. For workloads with predictable high volume, the Unlimited Node add-on provides flat-fee, RPS-tiered access from $149/month (25 RPS) to $3,199/month (500 RPS) with no per-request billing or overage. On the compliance side, Chainstack holds SOC 2 Type II (certified December 2025) and ISO 27001 (certified July 2026), with a 99.9% quarterly uptime SLA and service credits on Enterprise. [...] Robinhood’s own documentation names Alchemy, Quicknode, Blockdaemon, dRPC, and Validation Cloud as supported production RPC providers. Chainstack, RouteMesh, and GetBlock also support the chain independently of that list. For a standing free tier, Chainstack offers 3M request units per month and Alchemy offers 30M compute units; Quicknode is trial-only, while RouteMesh and dRPC offer free public/community endpoints without a full account.

Q: How do I migrate an existing Robinhood Chain integration to a new RPC provider? [...] ### Alchemy

Robinhood Chain is live on Alchemy for both mainnet and testnet, with the full Alchemy stack layered on top of plain JSON-RPC: webhooks for on-chain events, a bundler and Gas Manager API for ERC-4337, and data APIs for tokens, transfers, and NFTs. For teams building consumer apps that lean on account abstraction, this is a genuinely useful toolkit — the sponsored-gas and bundler endpoints map directly onto Robinhood Chain’s native ERC-4337 support.

Pricing is compute-unit (CU) based and method-weighted, with a generous 30M CU/month free tier that comfortably covers development and small production apps. Alchemy holds SOC 2 Type II but does not publish an ISO 27001 certification. It supports the Debug API on Robinhood Chain for tracing needs.

results.title: Best Free Tier RPCs for Web3 Builders in 2026 | Chainstack Blog
results.content:
On the free plan you get:

 3,000,000 request units per month — enough for a real prototype, not a toy
 25 requests per second steady throughput
 Global Node architecture — requests route to the nearest region automatically
 Support for 70+ protocols including Ethereum, Solana, Bitcoin, BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, TON, TRON, Starknet, Hyperliquid, and more
 Node analytics, node logs, and 2FA — all included [...] Most teams complete the switch in under 10 minutes. Sign up and create a project on Chainstack, deploy a node for your target network (Global, Trader, or Dedicated), and copy the new endpoint URL into your application or gateway in place of the old one. Chainstack’s endpoints follow standard JSON-RPC, so most codebases work with only a URL change. See the dedicated Quicknode and Alchemy migration guides.

What happens when I outgrow the free plan?

Extra usage on the Developer plan is metered at $20 per 1M request units — no forced upgrade. If you need more throughput, dedicated hardware, archive nodes, debug/trace API, or an SLA, the Growth plan unlocks those. You can also stay on Developer indefinitely if your app fits within 3M request units per month.

## Additional resources [...] Is there a truly free RPC provider with no credit card?

Yes. Chainstack’s Developer plan is free with no credit card required and no time limit — it’s a permanent plan, not a trial. It includes 3M request units per month, WebSockets, a private geo-balanced endpoint, MEV protection by default, and a free MCP server for AI agents. Some other providers advertise free tiers too, but signup flows and card requirements vary — always check before you commit. Sign up here.

Does Quicknode have a free tier?

No. Quicknode offers a 30-day free trial with 10M credits and 15 req/s. After 30 days, if you don’t upgrade to a paid plan (starting at $49/mo), your account is deactivated and your endpoints stop working. There is no permanent free tier.

results.title: Dedicated node RPC pricing in 2026 | Chainstack Blog
results.content:
Two more worth flagging even without a market figure to compare against: Robinhood Chain and Tempo are both available on Dedicated Node and come in cheap on their own. On Chainstack’s pricing calculator, Robinhood Chain (mainnet, full, ~550GB) comes out to $569.40/month; Tempo (mainnet, archive, ~500GB) to $547.50/month. Not a “cheaper than market” claim — just a real, checkable number on its own.

### Or skip the subscription entirely: Chainstack Self-Hosted [...] That figure is for an Ethereum full node on the Pro plan with ~2TB of storage, matching Chainstack’s documented steady-state requirement for Ethereum Mainnet (Reth + Prysm). Storage and compute needs vary a lot by chain — archive nodes and heavier chains will cost more; lighter chains meaningfully less.

Can I get a dedicated node on Chainstack’s Developer (free) plan?

No — Dedicated Node requires a Pro, Business, or Enterprise plan ($199/month and up). The free Developer plan gives you shared Global Nodes access instead.

How reliable are third-party estimates for competitor dedicated pricing?

Take them as a range, not a quote. Different trackers report different numbers because the actual price is negotiated per customer, so any published range reflects that spread, not a fixed rate. [...] Chainstack is the exception: Dedicated Node pricing is a published formula — a $199/month Pro plan (required to unlock the feature), plus from $0.50/hour compute, plus $0.01 per 20GB/hour storage. You can build the exact monthly number yourself before signing up — no sales call required to find out what you’d owe.

results.content:
Testnet ETH is available from the Chainstack Robinhood Chain testnet faucet. The free Developer plan includes 3M request units per month at 25 RPS, enough to prototype and validate an integration. Debug and trace APIs require a paid plan and a Global Node.

Prefer to work from an AI assistant? The Chainstack MCP server lets you deploy nodes and request testnet funds from a chat prompt in Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini, or Windsurf.

## Which Chainstack deployment models support Robinhood Chain?

Chainstack offers Robinhood Chain through three deployment models from a single account: shared Global Nodes, isolated Dedicated Nodes, and Chainstack Self-Hosted for teams that run nodes on their own infrastructure. [...] ## Getting started with Robinhood Chain on Chainstack

Production applications need a provider endpoint. Robinhood describes its public endpoint as rate limited and not recommended for production use, so anything moving past testing should not depend on it.

Start with Chainstack: deploy a Robinhood Chain node in about two minutes on the free Developer plan (3M request units per month), then move to a paid Global Node for production traffic, or to a Dedicated Node or Chainstack Self-Hosted when the workload needs isolation or full control over where data lives.
